'''Burt James Totaro''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (b. 1967), is an American [[mathematician]], currently a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], specializing in [[algebraic geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]].

== Education and early life ==
Totaro participated in the [[Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth]] while in grade school and enrolled at [[Princeton University]] in 1980 at the age of thirteen, becoming the youngest freshman in its history.<ref name=paw>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AxNbAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA54|title= Princeton Alumni Weekly|year= 1980}}</ref> He scored a perfect 800 on the math portion and a 690 on the verbal portion of the [[SAT-I]] exam at the age of 12.<ref name=paw/> He graduated in 1984 and went on to graduate school at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], receiving his [[Ph.D.]] in 1989.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|32036}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Since 2009, he has been one of three managing editors of the journal ''[[Compositio Mathematica]]'';<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.compositio.nl/editors.html|title=Editorial Board of Compositio Mathematica}}</ref> he is also on the editorial boards of [[Forum of Mathematics| Forum of Mathematics, Pi and Sigma]], the [[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]], and the [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]].  In 2012, he became a Professor in the UCLA Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/sites/default/files/newsletter/nl2012.pdf | title = UCLA Department of Mathematics newsletter}}</ref>

Totaro's work is influenced by the [[Hodge conjecture]], and is based on the connections and application of topology to algebraic geometry.  His work has applications in a number of diverse areas of mathematics, from [[representation theory]] to [[Lie theory]] and [[group cohomology]].<ref name=camel/>

===Selected works===
*{{cite journal|last=Totaro|first= Burt|title = Configuration spaces of algebraic varieties|journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] | volume= 35 |year=1996|issue= 4| pages=1057–1067|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(95)00058-5|mr=1404924|doi-access=free}}
*{{Cite book |last=Totaro |first=Burt |year=2014 |title=Group Cohomology and Algebraic Cycles |location=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-01577-7 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/9781107015777 }}

==Recognition==
In 2000, he was elected [[Lowndean Professor of Astronomy and Geometry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. In the same year, he was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations00/totaro.html Citation for Burt Totaro] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012060504/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations00/totaro.html |date=October 12, 2007 }}</ref>

In 2009, Totaro was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref name=camel>{{cite web | url = http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/news/dp/2009051501 | title = Cambridge academics elected as Fellows of the Royal Society | publisher = Cambridge University news | date = 2009-05-16 | accessdate = 2009-05-16 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090521091552/http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/news/dp/2009051501 | archive-date = 2009-05-21 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He was included in the 2019 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to algebraic geometry, Lie theory and cohomology and their connections and for service to the profession".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2019 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2018-11-07}}</ref>
